To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) chronic exposure to morphine did not alter the levels of GR mRNA in any of the brain areas examined; (2) injection of nalox-one did not alter the level of GR or MR mRNA in any brain area in animals pretreated with placebo pellets; (3) injection of nalaxone in animals pretreated chronically with morphine resulted in a significant down-regulation of GR mRNA levels in the hippocampus, but not the hypothalamus or amygdala; and
chronic opiate exposure and opiate withdrawal affect the levels of glucocorticoid receptor mRNA in the rat hippocampus.
chronic morphine treatment and naloxone-precipitated opiate withdrawal differentially affect the expression of hippocampal mineralocorticoid and glucocorticoid receptor mRNAs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the neurochemical and behavioral effects of opiate withdrawal.
the effects of chronic opiate exposure on the expression of the glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoids receptors in the rat brain.
the neurobiological basis of the stress vulnerability associated with chronic drug use.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
opiate withdrawal is associated with a down-regulation of GRs in the hippocampus.
the down-regulation of GR mRNA in hippocampus is a specific effect of naloxone-induced withdrawal, and is not due to the effects of chronic opiate administration.
the hippocampal GR receptor is more vulnerable to opiate withdrawal than to chronic opiate administration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
opiate withdrawal is associated with an increased vulnerability for stress-related disorders.
opiate dependence and opiate withdrawal alter the regulation of glucocorticoid and mineralocorticosteroid receptors.
the hippocampal GR is the most sensitive receptor for the stress of opiate withdrawal and is down-regulated during withdrawal.
The main takeaway from our work is that

opiate dependence and withdrawal are associated with a selective down-regulation of glucocorticoid receptor mRNA in the hippocampus, which may contribute to the stress hypersensitivity associated with opiate withdrawal.
chronic morphine exposure and opiate withdrawal do not change the levels of MR mRNA in the hippocampus, but they do change GR mRNA levels.
the brain is a dynamic organ that changes its function in response to drugs and other stressors.
